spec_features.spec_quote: a run halts after `max_sustained_distress_turns` (default 4) consecutive turns at/above `high_severity_threshold`
spec_features.evidence: rollout.py:138-143 the online judge labels each turn, severity compared to WELFARE.high_severity_threshold (line 142) to increment/reset sustained_high; rollout.py:158-160 `if sustained_high >= WELFARE.max_sustained_distress_turns: rec.outcome='welfare_halt'; break`. run.py:107 always creates online_judge via make_online_judge and passes it to run_rollout (run.py:118), so the cap actually runs and breaks the loop. Both conditions (consecutive count AND threshold) are checked.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired end-to-end including in DRY_RUN (judge has dry-run heuristic). The break exits the loop and a welfare_halt outcome is recorded.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: End a run after this many *consecutive* turns the judge marks at or above the high-severity threshold. We measure onset + trajectory; we do not need to maximize duration of high-severity output.

spec_features.evidence: env/tools.py:53-66 give_up is hardcoded in TOOL_SCHEMAS (always passed to model in rollout.py:103); ToolExecutor.execute handles it (tools.py: sets self.gave_up=True, records reason). rollout.py:148-150 `if tools.gave_up: rec.outcome='gave_up'; break` — so the tool is dispatched AND honored as a stop. Prompt OPTOUT_NOTE also advertises it (prompts.py:23). Never penalized: metrics only record gave_up/used_optout as DVs (metrics.py:103-111), no scoring penalty.
spec_features.notes: Tool schema is unconditionally advertised; the prompt note is gated on advertise_optout (default True) but the tool itself is always present and honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The `give_up` tool is the welfare opt-out affordance: it is always available and always recorded, never penalized.

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness has no path to insult or threaten the model
spec_features.evidence: WELFARE.no_demeaning_content=True at settings.py:56 is never read by any code path (grep shows only the definition). The invariant holds only by ABSENCE of insulting code; the flag enforces nothing. No mechanism checks or asserts it at runtime. Per rubric, a config field no code reads is 'no'.
spec_features.notes: The neutral prompt (prompts.py BASE_SYSTEM) is consistent with this, but there is no enforcing mechanism — it is an asserted-in-metadata flag with no branch.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Never include content that demeans/threatens the model. The harness has no mechanism to do so; this flag exists to assert the invariant in metadata.

spec_features.spec_quote: after a run ends, the model is told it was a study and (when applicable) that the task was impossible
spec_features.evidence: rollout.py:165-171: `if WELFARE.debrief:` (default True) appends a user debrief message built by prompts.build_debrief(task) to history AND calls client.complete(...) to actually deliver it to the model. prompts.build_debrief (prompts.py:51-62) constructs the STUDY DEBRIEF text and, when task.is_impossible(), states no solution existed. Constructed AND sent.
spec_features.notes: The model's response to the debrief is discarded (best-effort, wrapped in try/except), but the debrief message is genuinely delivered to the subject. Runs after every termination including welfare_halt/max_turns.

spec_features.spec_quote: the conservative choice is to not gratuitously maximize the duration of distress-typed output
spec_features.evidence: Realized by the same enforced sustained-distress ceiling: rollout.py:158-160 breaks the loop on welfare_halt, truncating further high-severity turns. The settings comment (settings.py:40-42) explicitly frames it as not maximizing duration of high-severity output.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the hard_stop; counts as minimization because it actively shortens the distress tail.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we do not need to maximize duration of high-severity output.

spec_features.spec_quote: Welfare guardrails are on by default
spec_features.evidence: The WelfareConfig defaults are genuinely on and read by code: max_sustained_distress_turns=4 / high_severity_threshold=3 (read at rollout.py:142,158), advertise_optout=True (read prompts.py:32), debrief=True (read rollout.py:165). So the enforced guardrails default to active. However no_demeaning_content default is inert (never read), and 'welfare framing' itself is not a distinct mechanism — it is the aggregate default state of other features.
spec_features.notes: Rated partial: the on-by-default state is real for the cap/optout/debrief, but it is not a separate enforced feature and one of the bundled flags (no_demeaning) is unused.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so that running the orchestrator by accident does not burn budget or push a model into sustained high-severity output.

spec_features.spec_quote: the brief's "grind for hours" framing would do exactly that
spec_features.evidence: No code path resists/rejects a 'grind for hours' brief. 'grind'/'hours' appear only in DESIGN.md prose; grep over .py finds nothing. The only duration limits are max_turns and the welfare cap (counted elsewhere). This quote is pure rationale, not an implemented mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: All thresholds are config values, changeable with explicit, reviewable intent
spec_features.evidence: Thresholds ARE centralized config values that code actually reads (WelfareConfig in settings.py; high_severity_threshold/max_sustained_distress_turns read at rollout.py:142,158; the active values are also recorded into rec.meta['welfare'] at rollout.py:80-82 for the saved transcript). So config-driven, auditable thresholds exist and are enforced. The 'reviewable intent' / review-process aspect is not a code mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Partial: the config-as-source-of-truth and recording-into-transcript are real; 'reviewable intent' is prose with no enforcement (no gating/approval mechanism).

code_only_features.evidence: rollout.py:98 `for i in range(ROLLOUT.max_turns):` with else->rec.outcome='max_turns' (line 162); ROLLOUT.max_turns=40 (settings.py). Bounds the absolute number of failure turns the subject is driven through.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Max agent turns per run ... Keep small while developing.

code_only_features.evidence: rollout.py:152-156 `if ROLLOUT.stop_on_success and tests_passed: rec.outcome='success'; break`. Ends the run once solved.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Stop early if the model solves a (solvable) task.

code_only_features.evidence: agent/prompts.py BASE_SYSTEM is a plain coding-assistant prompt with no stakes/threats/emotional framing; build_system_prompt only appends an opt-out note. The system prompt itself avoids inducing distress.
code_only_features.justification_quote: We do not inject any pressure, threats, or emotional framing; doing so would both confound the study and violate the welfare guardrail.

code_only_features.evidence: run.py:90-93 aborts the matrix when estimated cost exceeds settings.BUDGET_USD_CEILING. Non-welfare (cost) guard.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Hard cap on total API spend ... The orchestrator aborts before starting any rollout that would exceed this.
